newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF sale terms to be set in early Jan.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF sale terms to be set in early Jan.

text.p: The French government will decide on the terms of a privatisation of Thomson-CSF in early January, a source at the prime minister's office said on Thursday.

The government wants to sell its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF in the early part of 1997, separate from loss-making consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia, to speed up the privatisation of parent Thomson SA electronics group.
"The decision will not be taken before January," the source said.
The source said the delay in the decision, which had been expected either Friday or early next week, was due to the approaching Christmas holidays and the departure of staff.

The government suspended the privatisation through private placement of Thomson SA on December 4 because an independent privatisation commission did not approve of the sale of Thomson Multimedia to Korean firm Daewoo Electronics.
In its original sale plan, the government was to sell Thomson to French books-to-missile conglomerate Lagadere which would sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo.
A debate about the terms of the new sale has arisen since the suspension, which caused a furore in Korea where it was seen as discriminatory.
Senior officials at Thomson-CSF want a share flotation, while the head of Lagardere unit Matra Defence Espace has said a market float of Thomson-CSF would weaken and possibly break it apart.

A source close to Thomson-CSF on Thursday confirmed a report in Le Monde that senior directors of Thomson-CSF wrote to Prime Minister Alain Juppe to ask for a decision to use a market flotation instead of a private sale.
An official at the Prime Minister's office later said it had received notice of the directors' wish for a flotation but declined to comment on the move.
